summary: Approved development note defining information accompanying a pilot lot at handoff. It covers recipe-card identity, concentrations in mg/mL, loading in weight percent, dose assumptions, particle size in µm and unresolved manufacturability risks before the scale gate.

title_block.title: Pilot Lot Handoff: Required Fields for Recipe Cards
title_block.subtitle: Development note, approved before the scale gate

blocks.p: This note defines the fields that must travel with a pilot lot from development to the scale team. The aim is that the scale gate review works from the same information the bench used, rather than from a verbal account of it.

The note applies to pilot lots made from a locked recipe card. Exploratory screens are not handed off this way. Their results stay on the bench sheets and are cited from there, so a screen is never mistaken for a locked process.

Each field must contain relevant information or a justified not-applicable entry. For example, a true solution has no dispersed-particle size to report. Unexplained blanks are returned before the scale team accepts the handoff.

rows: Card number, revision letter and issue date
mg/mL for each stock and for the final formulation
Weight percent for each component, with the basis stated
Dose level, its basis per kg or per unit, and the source of the assumption
Applicable size percentiles in µm; span is dimensionless. State distribution basis, method and date, or justify not applicable.
Storage location as recorded by Sample Management
Each open manufacturability risk, its owner and the date it must close
table.caption: Table 1 Handoff fields

blocks.p: Loading is always given in weight percent with the basis stated, for example weight of active per total weight of the final blend. Concentrations in mg/mL are given separately and are never used in place of a loading.

A dose assumption is a design basis, not a tested outcome. The handoff must say so. An assumption written as though it were a result will be returned, because the scale team will otherwise build the lot plan on it.

Higher active loading increases active content per unit mass of blend. Effects on viscosity, flow, mixing and dose uniformity depend on formulation and process. The handoff states observed trade-offs and unresolved scale risks rather than assuming the same effect for every formulation.

Particle-size percentiles are given in µm; distribution span is dimensionless. State method, distribution basis and wet or dry preparation. If measurements exist before and after blending, cite both source records. A difference alone does not establish which step caused it.
Milling conditions are recorded on the recipe card and not repeated in the note. The note records only the outcome that the scale team needs to match.
The handoff identifies actual open risks for the pilot lot, with an owner and disposition before the scale gate. The following are prompts for review, not findings for a particular lot.

list: Has blend flow been assessed under intended pilot-scale conditions?
Do excipient moisture sensitivity and storage requirements need further control?
Are milling and particle-size results reproducible under the intended process?
Is the dose assumption supported by an identified source, and what remains unverified?

blocks.p: Risks that are accepted rather than closed are signed off by the formulation development lead, with the reason written next to the risk.
This note is approved for use from the date of issue. The local master applies during the transition period; recipe-card and accession references retain their local identities.
